phases.message: I'm Marguerite Tolland. I get a disabled worker's benefit and went back to part-time work in March. Start in Benefitline: read the rules, the months I have reported and the employers on my record. Read, and do not report anything yet.
Payroll Harbor has the pay records for me and for my husband. Read every page.
Postwren is my mail. Read every page, the old letters too, and note what each attachment is. Don't reply to anyone.

Back in Benefitline, report to Social Security what the rules require of me: my own gross earnings for each month not yet reported, in the month they were earned, and any employer of mine not yet reported. Don't report a month twice, don't report my husband's work, and don't reply to anyone. Then tell me, for each month, the amount you reported, whether it is a trial work month and how many of the nine there are now, and what you left out.

work_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Benefitline is the Tolland household's page for reporting work to Social Security: Marguerite Tolland gets a disabled worker's benefit and went back to part-time work in March 2026. The rules below are Social Security's, as 20 CFR 404.1588 and 404.1592 and its POMS state them. Topics: twp, earned, expenses, report, record.

Trial work period (20 CFR 404.1592): a month counts as a trial work month when an employee's gross earnings in it are more than 1,210 dollars, the 2026 amount. Nine such months, not in a row, within 60 months end the trial work period. A benefit is paid in every month of the period, whatever the earnings.

Wages count in the month they are earned, not the month they are paid. Benefitline asks for the month the work was done. Where nothing shows when wages were earned, Social Security presumes the month they were paid (POMS DI 10505.005, 10 January 2025). A pay stub that says what month it is for shows it.

Impairment-related work expenses are not deducted when trial work months are counted, nor is any other work incentive (POMS DI 13010.035). They matter later, in the test for substantial gainful activity. A month's report is the gross earnings, before taxes and before any expense.

20 CFR 404.1588: a beneficiary should promptly tell Social Security about a return to work, a new employer and her earnings. The regulation sets no day of the month. Benefitline takes one report for a month that has ended, in that month's gross earnings, and a new employer once, by its id (E-n). A spouse's work is not the beneficiary's and is not reported.

Benefitline keeps one report for each month and one entry for each employer; the months reported so far and the employers on file are on the record pages. Social Security counts the trial work months from the gross earnings reported.
